Porting from Pyrogram
=====================

Kurigram is a drop-in replacement by import name only. ``import pyrogram`` keeps working, and
most code keeps working with it, but the surface has moved a long way since Pyrogram stopped:
Pyrogram {reference_version} exposes {reference_methods} public methods, Kurigram {tree_version}
exposes {tree_methods}, and {added_methods} of those are new. This page is the part of that
difference which can break code you already wrote.

It is generated by diffing the two trees, and rewritten every time the documentation is built,
so it describes the version of Kurigram you are reading rather than the one somebody wrote it
for. The reference is commit ``{reference_commit}``, which is Pyrogram {reference_version}, the
last release that project made.

-----

The layer gap
-------------

Pyrogram {reference_version} speaks Telegram's API layer {reference_layer}; Kurigram speaks layer
{tree_layer}.

That only matters directly if you call :doc:`raw API methods <../telegram/functions/index>`. The
:mod:`pyrogram.raw` package is generated from the schema, so constructors that Telegram renamed,
re-flagged or retired between the two layers change name, gain fields or disappear outright, and
no deprecation period covers them. High-level methods absorb the churn; a
``client.invoke(raw.functions....)`` call does not.

-----

Names that are gone
-------------------

{removed}

Two more names moved out of :mod:`pyrogram.storage`. Pyrogram had a ``FileStorage`` and a
``MemoryStorage``; Kurigram has one :class:`~pyrogram.storage.SQLiteStorage` that takes an
``in_memory`` flag, so an import of either old name fails. Nothing changes for the ordinary case,
because ``Client(..., in_memory=True)`` was and still is how you ask for it.

-----

Names that still work
---------------------

These were renamed, and the Pyrogram spelling is kept as an alias. Nothing has to change, and
new code should use the right-hand column.

{aliases}

-----

Parameters that are gone
------------------------

These methods still exist and still do what they did, but they no longer accept the parameters
listed here. Passing one raises :exc:`TypeError` at the call site, which at least means you find
out immediately.

{dropped_parameters}

Most of that table is one change. Every ``Message.reply_*`` bound method has lost ``quote`` and
``reply_to_message_id``, and the bound methods now always reply to the message they are bound to.
Under Pyrogram, ``quote`` was a boolean defaulting to ``True`` in groups and ``False`` in private
chats, so the same call replied in one place and did not in the other.

.. code-block:: python

    # Pyrogram: reply, or not, depending on `quote`.
    await message.reply_photo(photo, quote=True)
    await message.reply_photo(photo, quote=False)

.. code-block:: python

    # Kurigram: the bound method always replies.
    await message.reply_photo(photo)

    # To send without replying, send to the chat instead.
    await client.send_photo(message.chat.id, photo)

``quote`` still exists, and that is the trap: it is now a field of
:class:`~pyrogram.types.ReplyParameters`, and it is a ``str`` rather than a ``bool``. It carries
the exact substring of the replied-to message that Telegram should show as the quote. Reply
targeting in general moved to that type:

.. code-block:: python

    # Pyrogram.
    await client.send_message(chat_id, "text", reply_to_message_id=message.id)

.. code-block:: python

    # Kurigram.
    await client.send_message(
        chat_id,
        "text",
        reply_parameters=ReplyParameters(message_id=message.id),
    )

Three more entries in that table are worth spelling out:

- :meth:`~pyrogram.Client.send_poll` and :meth:`~pyrogram.types.Message.reply_poll` renamed
  ``correct_option_id`` to ``correct_option_ids`` and take a list, because a quiz may now have
  more than one right answer. ``explanation_parse_mode`` and ``explanation_entities`` went with
  it.
- :meth:`~pyrogram.types.Message.edit_text` replaced ``disable_web_page_preview`` with
  ``link_preview_options``, which is where every link-preview setting now lives.
- :meth:`~pyrogram.Client.run` no longer takes a coroutine. Pyrogram let you write
  ``app.run(main())`` to run one to completion; write ``asyncio.run(main())`` instead. Kurigram's
  ``run()`` starts the client, idles and stops, and its own parameters are keyword-only.

-----

Calls that bind by position
---------------------------

Kurigram inserted parameters into the middle of these signatures rather than appending them, so
a Pyrogram call that passed arguments positionally binds the wrong values to the wrong names.
Nothing raises: the call succeeds and does the wrong thing.

{positional}

Everything Kurigram appended after the last of Pyrogram's own parameters is left out of this
table, because appending cannot move an argument. If you call any of these positionally past the
count given, switch to keyword arguments before upgrading. This is the change most likely to
produce a bug that looks like a Telegram problem.

-----

Defaults that changed
---------------------

The same call now behaves differently, or a parameter that could be omitted no longer can be.
Parameters that merely gained a default are left out: they cannot break a call that already
passed them.

{defaults}

{enum_members}

-----

What did not change
-------------------

The :class:`~pyrogram.Client` constructor is purely additive. It grew from 25 parameters to 41,
and not one was removed, renamed or given a different default, so an existing ``Client(...)``
call is safe as written.

Type annotations changed nearly everywhere, and none of it is a porting concern. The tree moved
from ``typing.Union`` and ``typing.List`` to the ``|`` and ``list[...]`` spellings, and optional
parameters that were annotated as if they were required now say ``| None``. Those differences are
deliberately left out of the tables above: acting on any of them would be work for nothing.

-----

What this page cannot tell you
------------------------------

Everything above is derived from the two trees' signatures. Four things a signature diff cannot
see, and they are the ones most likely to bite:

- **Session files migrate forward, once.** Pyrogram wrote schema version 3; Kurigram writes
  version 7 and upgrades a version 3 file in place the first time it opens it. The upgraded file
  does not open in Pyrogram again, so copy it before the first run if you intend to keep both
  libraries working against the same account.
- **Python 3.10 is the floor.** Pyrogram {reference_version} declared ``~=3.7``.
- **A method that kept its signature may not have kept its behaviour.** The parser, the
  dispatcher and the update handling have all been rewritten since {reference_version}, and
  nothing in a signature records that.
- **The set of update types is much larger.** A filter or a handler written against Pyrogram's
  update types will not see the ones Telegram added after layer {reference_layer}.

If you hit something this page should have listed, it is worth an issue: the tables are
generated, so a gap in them is a gap in the generator and can be fixed once for everyone.
